response.text: Hello! 😊 I am your WuWa Config Patcher AI Assistant. I can assist you with 1-Click Patching, Live Config Editing, CVar Section Guards, C# Environment, Shizuku & Root elevation, Log Decryption, CVar Analyzer, Hardware recommendations, and troubleshooting game bugs or crashes!

WuWa Config Patcher (v1.5.1) is an open-source Android utility developed by Arglax (io.github.arglax.configpatcher). It is 100% free and open source. Releases and updates are hosted on GitHub at Arglax/WuWa-Mobile-Config-Patcher.

1-Click Preset Patching Workflow (Tab 1: ConfigScreen):
1. Select Repository: Choose Arglax (Default), Custom Online Repository, or Local Repository.
2. Sync: Tap Sync Files & Refresh (or pull down to refresh) to extract archives via ZipExtractor.kt.
3. Select Preset: Browse categories (STABLE, PERFORMANCE, HIGH_VISUAL, COMMUNITY). Nested INIs in deep subfolders are auto-detected by ConfigScanner.kt.
4. Patch: Tap 1-Click Patch. It creates a backup in app_main_storage/backups/ and injects configs via elevated Shizuku/Root IPC.
• Per-File Patching: Tap the Gear Icon (⚙️) next to 1-Click Patch (AdvancedPatchDialog.kt) to select individual INI files.
• Tap Launch Game to launch Wuthering Waves immediately.

Live Config Editor (Tab 2: EditorScreen):
Supports editing Engine.ini (Gold), DeviceProfiles.ini (Gold), and GameUserSettings.ini (Green) with 0ms in-memory tab switching.
• Smart Mode: Sectioned UI cards. Features Sort A-Z (sortSmartSectionsAlphabetically()), Auto-Fix / Auto-Categorize, value steppers (with negative number support), and multi-select bulk delete.
• Text Mode: Syntax-highlighted raw editor with line numbers, Isolation Search Mode, Find & Replace, and font slider (8sp-24sp). Includes defensive OffsetMapping clamping to prevent crashes with Windows \r\n line breaks.
• One-Line Mode: Rapid dropdown selector with live buffer preview card before saving.

Engine CVar Section Guards (CVarSectionGuard.kt):
Unreal Engine ignores misplaced CVars. The patcher enforces canonical section headers:
• r. CVars → [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings]
• s. CVars → [/Script/Engine.StreamingSettings]
• gc. CVars → [/Script/Engine.GarbageCollectionSettings]
• n. / p. network CVars → [/Script/Engine.NetworkSettings]
• cook. CVars → [/Script/UnrealEd.CookerSettings]
• General CVars → [SystemSettings] or [ConsoleVariables]

Protection Rules:
1. Misplaced lines & CVars= / +CVars= prefixes in Engine.ini are highlighted in bold Vibrant Red (#FF2222).
2. Tapping Save displays an Auto-Fix Sections remediation button that strips invalid prefixes and groups CVars into their canonical headers.
3. [Core.Paths], [Core.System], and [/Script/Engine.RendererOverrideSettings] are whitelisted and never moved or flagged.
4. DeviceProfiles.ini entries are automatically maintained as CVars=Key=Value without disturbing metadata pointers (BaseProfileName, DeviceScore).

Enabling C# Environment Scripting (Tab 2: Misc Patch):
Kuro Games built an experimental C# scripting runtime for Wuthering Waves that improves frame pacing, reduces CPU overhead, and speeds up asset streaming.

How to Enable:
1. Go to Editor Tab > Misc Patch subtab.
2. Check -ForceEnableCSharpEnvironment (and optionally -SkipSplash) and tap Patch. This pushes flags to .../files/UE4Game/Client/UE4CommandLine.txt.
3. Verification: Launch the game. An asterisk (*) at the end of the client version string on the splash screen confirms C# is active! In Utilities > Decrypted Log Explorer, search for Sharphereal entries.

⚠️ Hardware Note: Requires at least 8 GB RAM. On devices with less than 8 GB RAM, disable this flag to prevent memory pressure crashes.

Elevated Access Backends Hierarchy:
Android 11+ enforces Scoped Storage. WuWa Config Patcher supports 5 elevation backends:
• ROOT (Red #E35D6A): Native SU shell execution via topjohnwu libsu Core (v6.0.0).
• SHIZUKU (Green #47D764): Wireless Debugging / ADB IPC via rikka.shizuku.api (zero root needed).
• AXMANAGER (Blue #2AA37D): Axeron shell provider integration.
• SHIZUKU_UNAUTHORIZED (Orange #F7C948): Shizuku binder running, permission pending approval.
• NONE (Gray #A8B4AF): No elevated backend detected.

Setting Up Shizuku:
1. Enable Developer Options (tap Build Number 7 times in Android Settings).
2. Enable USB Debugging and Wireless Debugging.
3. Open Shizuku, tap Pairing > Pair device with pairing code, and enter the 6-digit code.
4. Tap Start in Shizuku, then return to WuWa Config Patcher and grant permission.
• Xiaomi / HyperOS / MIUI Fix: You must enable "USB Debugging (Security Settings)" in Developer Options!

Analyze Config (CVarAnalyzer.kt — Tab 3: Advanced Subtab):
Cross-checks active on-device INI CVars against decrypted Client.log execution blocks near the end of the log.
• KPIs: Displays Total CVars, Applied %, Failed count, and Deleted/Ignored count.
• Status Codes:
- APPLIED: CVar value matched the executed engine value.
- FAILED / UNREAD: Game engine skipped or did not read the line.
- DELETED BY GAME: Game stripped or rejected the variable.
• Features: Filter by Status (All / Applied / Failed / Deleted), File Filter (Engine.ini / DeviceProfiles.ini), frozen left CVar column table, and Collapsible Smart Insights panel.

CVar Bank & Reference Library (Tab 3: Advanced Subtab):
A searchable library of 1000+ CVars loaded asynchronously from assets/alteriax_cvars.txt (AlteriaX Pastebin) and official Unreal Engine documentation.

Features:
• Source Filters: Filter by All Sources, AlteriaX Pastebin, or Unreal Engine Docs.
• Display: Toggle between Card View and high-density Table View.
• Extract Web CVars: Paste raw text or web pages to dynamically parse and import new CVars into your local database.
• Send to Editor: Tap "Send to Editor" beside any CVar to instantly jump to Config Editor and insert it into Smart Mode under its canonical section!

Forbidden CVars (Updated as of WuWa v3.6):
These CVars cause engine rejection, black screens, or game crashes when injected on mobile. The patcher provides Strip Forbidden (ForbiddenCvarStripper.kt) in Utilities > Advanced to auto-strip all forbidden CVars with 1 tap!

Reference Link: Arglax Mobile-WuWa-Config forbidden_cvars.txt

Forbidden CVars List:
• Kuro.CppEffectsystem.UseLowMemoryPlayerEffectLruCapacity
• r.AFME.Enable, r.AsyncComputePSO, r.DetailMode, r.FEstimation.Option
• r.Kuro.SkeletalMesh.LODDistanceScale, r.Kuro.TexturePool.ExtraBudgetMB, r.KuroFI.Enable, r.KuroMaterialQualityLevel
• r.LightMaxDrawDistanceScale, r.MaterialQualityLevel, r.MFRC.Enable, r.MipMapLODBias, r.Mobile.DeviceEvaluation, r.MobileContentScaleFactor
• r.ParallelInitViews, r.RayTracing.LimitDevice, r.ScreenPercentage, r.ScreenSizeCullRatioFactor, r.SecondaryScreenPercentage.GameViewport
• r.Shadow.DistanceScale, r.Shadow.MaxCSMResolution, r.Shadow.MaxResolution
• r.streaming.AllowExtendedPoolSize, r.Streaming.Boost, r.Streaming.CPUReadback, r.Streaming.DistancePriority.Texture2DArrayPriority, r.streaming.ExtendedPoolSizeForceAllMipsThresholdPercentage, r.streaming.ExtendedPoolSizeThresholdPercentage, r.Streaming.KuroExtraPoolSize, r.Streaming.LimitPoolSizeTOVRAM, r.streaming.MaxExtendedPoolSizePercentage, r.streaming.MaxExtendedPoolsizeVRAMPercentage, r.Streaming.MaxNumTexturesTostreamPerFrame, r.Streaming.MaxTempMemoryAllowed, r.Streaming.MaxTempMemoryAllowedForTexture2DArray, r.Streaming.MinBoost, r.Streaming.MinMipForSplitRequest, r.Streaming.PoolSize, r.Streaming.PoolSizeExtraForTexture2DArray, r.Streaming.Texture2DArrayStreamOutHysteresis, r.Streaming.UseAllMips, r.Streaming.UseAsyncCPUReadback, r.Streaming.UseFixedPoolsize
• r.Streamline.DLSSG.RetainResourceswhenoff, r.TextureGroup.Landscape.TextureLODBias, r.ViewDistanceScale, r.VolumetricFog, r.VRS.EnableMaterial, r.VRS.EnableMesh, s.PriorityAsyncLoadingExtraTime

Popular & Recommended CVars for Wuthering Waves:
• r.MobileContentScaleFactor = 0.8 to 1.5 (Section: [SystemSettings] — scales 3D render resolution; use lower values for FPS boosts).
• r.ShadowQuality = 0 to 3 (Section: [SystemSettings] — shadow map detail).
• r.BloomQuality = 0 or 1 (Section: [SystemSettings] — bloom/glare post-processing).
• r.VSync = 0 or 1 (Section: [SystemSettings] — vertical sync toggle).
• r.VolumetricFog = 0 (Section: [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings] — disables heavy volumetric fog).
• s.AsyncLoadingThreadEnabled = 1 (Section: [/Script/Engine.StreamingSettings] — asynchronous background asset streaming).

Important: Avoid adding variables from the Forbidden CVars list, and always use Auto-Fix Sections in Smart Mode to ensure canonical placement.

Hardware & RAM Recommendations:
• 8 GB Physical RAM or higher: Recommended for Extreme / High Visual presets and Kuro's C# Environment.
• 6 GB Physical RAM: Best suited for STABLE or PERFORMANCE presets.
• Under 6 GB RAM: Recommended to run Vanilla defaults or Low presets to avoid low-memory kills during scene changes.

Check Your Device Hardware:
Go to Utilities > Common > Get Device Info (DeviceStatsCollector.kt). It extracts your exact GPU renderer, Vulkan driver version, physical RAM, CPU core topology, and game-evaluated Device Score directly from Client.log!

Utilities & Log Diagnostics (Tab 3: Common & Advanced):
• Decrypted Log Explorer: Real-time viewer for Client.log with line numbers and filter chips (LogConfig, GameThread, Sharphereal, LogInit, LogTemp, Vulkan, RHI).
• Log Decryptor (LogDecryptor.kt): Decrypts obfuscated logs using Scheme A (XOR 0xA5/0xEF), Scheme B (XOR 0x55), or Plaintext fallback.
• Delete Logs: Runs elevated rm -rf on .../Saved/Logs/ to reclaim gigabytes of storage.
• Export & Sharing (PatchExporter.kt): Compresses active INIs into a custom-named ZIP or exports to SAF folders.
• Main Storage (MainStorageReaderDialog.kt): Inspects snapshots in context.filesDir/app_main_storage/ with 1-tap Restore Backup.

Settings Screen & Danger Zone (Tab 4: SettingsScreen):
• Danger Zone (3-Step Guarded Actions):
- Delete Shaders (DeleteShadersDialog.kt): Wipes Vulkan (VulkanProgramBinaryCache) or OpenGL (ProgramBinaryCache) compiled shader caches to resolve graphic glitches and shader compile crashes after game updates.
- Clear App Cache & History: Wipes temporary repository zip caches and editor undo/redo snapshot stacks.
- Clear App Data & Exports: Complete factory reset for repository URLs and exports.
- Clear Activity Log: Erases context.filesDir/activity_log.txt.
• Quick Jumps: One-tap shortcuts to Developer Options, Wireless Debugging, Shizuku App, Axeron, and WuWaLab.

title: Remediation: Game Crashing, Lag, Stutter, or Black Screen

response.text:
Troubleshooting: Game Crashing, Black Screen, or Stuttering:
Follow these remediation steps in order:

Step 1: Revert to Clean Vanilla Defaults
Go to Utilities > Common > Vanilla mode and tap the red Revert to Vanilla button. This deletes modified Engine.ini, DeviceProfiles.ini, and Scalability.ini so Kuro Games factory defaults regenerate on launch.

Step 2: Delete Corrupted Shader Caches
Go to Settings > Danger Zone > Delete Shaders (DeleteShadersDialog.kt) and clear both Vulkan and OpenGL caches. Shader corruption often occurs following game version updates.

Step 3: Strip Forbidden CVars
Go to Utilities > Advanced Subtab > Strip Forbidden (ForbiddenCvarStripper.kt) and tap Auto Strip All.

Step 4: Check C# Environment & RAM Pressure
If your device has less than 8 GB RAM, open Editor > Misc Patch and uncheck -ForceEnableCSharpEnvironment.

Step 5: Still not resolved?
If the issue persists, open Support > Report a Bug (BugReportDialog.kt) to send your device diagnostics and activity_log.txt directly to developer Arglax on Discord or GitHub.

title: Remediation: Shizuku Not Working or Access NONE

response.text:
Troubleshooting: Elevated Access "NONE" or Shizuku Issues:
Follow these steps to restore elevated permissions:

Step 1: Check Shizuku Service Status
Open the Shizuku standalone app. Ensure it reports "Shizuku is running". If stopped, re-pair using Wireless Debugging and enter the 6-digit code.

Step 2: Xiaomi / HyperOS / MIUI Mandatory Fix
Inside Android Developer Options, you must enable "USB Debugging (Security Settings)" (requires Mi Account login). Without this, Xiaomi blocks Shizuku from executing file writes.

Step 3: Refresh or Revoke Permission
Go to Settings Tab > Application Info in WuWa Config Patcher and tap the Refresh icon. If still failing, open the Shizuku app, revoke permissions for WuWa Config Patcher, force stop the patcher, and reopen it to prompt approval again.

Step 4: Alternative Backends
If your device is rooted, tap Grant Root in Settings to use native SU via libsu.

Step 5: Still failing?
Report the issue to developer Arglax via Support > Report a Bug with your backend log.

title: Remediation: Vibrant Red CVars & Failed Section Checks

response.text:
Troubleshooting: Vibrant Red Text (#FF2222) & Misplaced CVars:

Step 1: Use 1-Tap Auto-Fix Sections
When saving in Config Editor, tap Auto-Fix Sections in the dialog. The patcher will automatically strip illegal CVars= prefixes from Engine.ini and route variables to canonical headers (e.g. r. to RendererSettings, s. to StreamingSettings).

Step 2: Verify in CVar Analyzer
After launching the game, open Utilities > Advanced > Analyze Config (CVarAnalyzer.kt). If a CVar shows DELETED BY GAME, Kuro's runtime explicitly stripped it because it is either protected, obsolete, or listed in the Forbidden CVars bank.

Step 3: Check Whitelisted Headers
Remember that [Core.Paths], [Core.System], and [/Script/Engine.RendererOverrideSettings] are whitelisted and never altered.

Bug Reporting & Creator Support (Tab 5: SupportScreen):
• Backend Activity Log: Every action, Shizuku IPC binder call, and exception is logged to context.filesDir/activity_log.txt by ActionLogger.kt. Inspect it in Utilities > View Backend Activity Log.
• Report a Bug Generator (BugReportDialog.kt): Tap "Report a Bug / Suggest a Feature" on the Support tab. It automatically packages device specs and recent logs to send directly to developer Arglax via Discord or GitHub Issues.
• Support Arglax: The application is 100% free and ad-free. You can donate directly via the in-app GCash / InstaPay QR dialog (GCashDialog.kt).

title: Manual Mode Guide (Old School File Managers)

response.text:
Manual Mode (Android 11–13 Fallback):
If unable to run Shizuku or Root:
1. Go to Utilities > Export & Sharing > Share Patch and extract the INIs.
2. Using FV File Explorer, ZArchiver, or MT Manager, copy the files to:
/storage/emulated/0/Android/data/<package>/files/UE4Game/Client/Client/Saved/Config/Android/

⚠️ Android 14 / 15 Note: Google has strictly locked down /Android/data/ access on newer OS versions. Shizuku or Root access is required on Android 14 and 15+.
